target_customer: Independent physician practices that need an EHR, practice management and billing system
problem: Electronic health records were clunky desktop software. drchrono built a native iPad EHR so doctors could chart on a tablet.
business_model: SaaS subscription for EHR and practice management, plus billing and revenue cycle services

founders.name: Michael Nusimow
founders.background_notes: College friend of Kivatinos at Stony Brook per search coverage.

competitors.name: Epic Canto
competitors.what: Planned iPad version of Epic's iPhone app Haiku, per June 2010 reporting

technical_complexity.rationale: A native iPad EHR with Meaningful Use certification, e-prescribing and later billing and integrations was standard software with heavy compliance requirements.

defensibility.rationale: EHR data and Meaningful Use certification create switching costs, but the iPad first angle was copyable by incumbents such as Epic and GE.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents built tablet clients. drchrono stayed independent for a decade and was bought by EverCommerce in November 2021 for about 182.5 million dollars.

market_need_then: The HITECH Act paid physicians up to 44,000 dollars for Meaningful Use of certified EHRs, and drchrono said its iPad app was certified in mid 2011, a regulation driven demand wave.

branding.domain_note: Uses drchrono.com per the company site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, practical and supportive, focus on patients not paperwork

rebrands.why: Brand folded into EverCommerce's EverHealth group after the acquisition

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found in the searches run.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognized name among iPad EHR users but no coverage of the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Expanded suite with patient check in, billing, telehealth and an app marketplace
pivots.why: Added OnPatient check in app in August 2011 and later a broader platform

outcome_analysis: drchrono rode the iPad launch and Meaningful Use incentives in 2011 with a tablet first EHR, raised small seed rounds from Yuri Milner and a 12 million dollar Series A in 2017, and was acquired by EverCommerce in November 2021 for roughly 182.5 million dollars. The sale price is modest relative to the capital and time, which suggests competition from larger EHR vendors capped the outcome.
notes: Deal price is 182.5 million dollars per EverCommerce's S-1, with 180 million and 181.9 million also reported. A 2011 raise is reported as 650K by TechCrunch and 675K elsewhere. ORIX Growth Capital financing of about 12 million growth and 20 million debt is reported without clear dates, so it is excluded from rounds. Aggregator totals of 36 to 148 million dollars conflict and are unreliable. Competitor search returned no athenahealth or Practice Fusion items. The Epic Canto source is an iMedicalApps 2011 review citing June 2010 plans.
